# Baselarte

> Baselarte (Baselarte Ltda.) is a software engineering and creative technology company. It builds systems, interfaces and infrastructure that are simple on the surface and rigorous underneath.

The public website is a landing page plus a notes section (an AWS study guide, the site's design system a GitHub-to-AWS OIDC CI/CD guide and Cloudflare/R2/SSL notes), available in English and Brazilian Portuguese (switchable on the page). There is no product, pricing, blog or contact form published yet; inquiries are by introduction only. Motto: "Non desistas. Non exieris."

## Principles

- Simplicity is a discipline, not a starting point.
- Fundamentals over fashion.
- Build only what is necessary, then make it excellent.
- Clarity over abstraction.

## Accountability

The site quotes an IBM internal training presentation (1979): "A computer can never be held accountable, therefore a computer must never make a management decision." Baselarte builds tools that help people decide, not tools that decide for them.

## Pages

- [Home](https://baselarte.com/): landing page describing the company, its principles.
- [Notes](https://baselarte.com/notas/): index of study notes.
- [AWS Notes](https://baselarte.com/notas/aws/): interactive AWS study guide (IAM, Organizations, VPC, ECS, RDS, S3, Route 53 and more) based on the official documentation, in English and Brazilian Portuguese.
- [GitHub to AWS with OIDC](https://baselarte.com/notas/github-aws-oidc/): CI/CD notes on deploying from GitHub Actions to AWS (ECR/ECS) with OIDC, for develop and production, based on the official docs.
- [Cloudflare notes](https://baselarte.com/notas/cloudflare/): buying and configuring a domain, R2 with presigned URLs (private/public buckets, CDN), SSL certificates and HTTPS to an AWS ALB, based on the official docs.
- [Software Engineering at Google notes](https://baselarte.com/notas/software-engineering-at-google/): book notes on time, scale and trade-offs, Hyrum's Law, testing, code review and continuous delivery.
- [AI Engineering notes](https://baselarte.com/notas/ai-engineering/): book notes on tokens, sampling, prompting, RAG, agents, evaluation, finetuning, inference and AI application architecture.
- [Grokking Algorithms notes](https://baselarte.com/notas/entendendo-algoritmos/): book notes on Big O notation, binary search, sorting, recursion, hash tables, graphs, Dijkstra, greedy algorithms, dynamic programming and k-nearest neighbours, with examples and code.
- [Terraform 80/20](https://baselarte.com/notas/terraform/): the 20% of Terraform that covers 80% of the work (workflow, HCL, state, modules, CI) plus a complete AWS walkthrough (remote state on S3, VPC, EC2, IAM, S3).
- [Kubernetes from zero: concepts, security and AWS](https://baselarte.com/notas/kubernetes/): what Kubernetes is and the problem it solves, the YAML files and their security options, small progressive labs with Docker (kind), and how to run it securely on AWS with EKS.
- [Observability: metrics, p95/p99, logs and traces](https://baselarte.com/notas/observability/): what observability is, the KPIs worth measuring, why p95 and p99 beat the average, how to add Prometheus and Grafana to a project, when you also need traces and logs (Jaeger, Loki, Elasticsearch), a hands-on Docker lab, and how to run it securely in production.
- [Attention Is All You Need, explained](https://baselarte.com/notas/attention-is-all-you-need/): a plain-language guide to the Transformer paper: queries, keys and values, scaled dot-product and multi-head attention with small worked numbers, positional encoding, the encoder-decoder architecture, masking, training, results and a runnable code example.
- [Open-source LLMs and AI agents: run, connect and deploy](https://baselarte.com/notas/llm-agents-open-source/): how much memory a model needs, running open-source models with Ollama, llama.cpp and vLLM, writing a tool-calling agent loop in plain Python, connecting agent and model through the OpenAI-compatible API and MCP, and renting a GPU in the cloud securely (SSH tunnel, no public ports). Also covers Chinese open-weights models (DeepSeek, Qwen, Kimi, GLM), ready-made agents (Hermes Agent, OpenHands, Aider, Goose, Cline) and RAG with Postgres and pgvector. Eleven hands-on activities with expected results.
- [Focus and attention: recovering from brain rot](https://baselarte.com/notas/focus-and-attention/): what research says about smartphones, short-form video and interruptions, the habit loop, and a four-week plan of practical exercises with expected results, each tied to a peer-reviewed source.
- [How Linux works](https://baselarte.com/notas/linux/): visual, exam-style guide to users and root, permissions, the file tree, commands, processes, networking, SSH, firewalls, terminal and web monitoring tools, and clearing shell history.
- [Cybersecurity for developers: where to start](https://baselarte.com/notas/cybersecurity-for-devs/): the entry point to the security series: the map of the field (red, blue, purple team, AppSec, cloud), core concepts (CIA, STRIDE, CVE/CWE/CVSS, ATT&CK), a five-stage study path, eight portfolio projects (scanning, CI security, a home SOC with Suricata and Wazuh, Sigma rules), where to learn, certifications, ethics and law, and a 90-day plan.
- [Security and networking lab](https://baselarte.com/notas/security-lab/): hands-on exercises on your own machines, covering sessions, nmap, SSH tunnels, self-hosted WireGuard VPNs (including full-tunnel, no-DNS-leak, kill-switch setups for public Wi-Fi), Wireshark, firewalls, a safe recon-tool overview, and Docker networking explained with a real-machine comparison.
- [Red team 80/20](https://baselarte.com/notas/red-team-80-20/): defensive-minded red team concepts — the attack lifecycle, social engineering and phishing simulation, SQL injection and XSS, reverse shells — each in a safe Docker lab (DVWA, Juice Shop, Gophish) with a named defence for every technique.
- [Sign-in and authentication: SSO, OAuth, OIDC and friends](https://baselarte.com/notas/auth-sso-oauth-oidc/): authentication vs. authorization, MFA and passkeys, SSO, OAuth 2.0, OpenID Connect, SAML, LDAP and Kerberos, a full "Sign in with Google" flow, and GitHub Actions to AWS with OIDC (no stored keys), with trust policy, workflow and common errors.
- [Secure web apps: headers, auth and AI agents](https://baselarte.com/notas/web-app-security/): HTTPS and security headers (HSTS, CSP with nonces, building your own middleware, Next.js and Nginx), cookie attributes, stateful sessions vs. stateless JWT (access + refresh tokens), CSRF, SQL injection and XSS from the builder's side, and AI agent security (prompt injection, excessive agency, MCP risks) per OWASP.
- [React state: Context API and Zustand](https://baselarte.com/notas/react-state/): from the official docs, prop drilling, createContext and useContext, the reducer + context pattern, Zustand stores and selectors, per-request stores in Next.js, and when to use each.
- [Idempotency: safe retries for APIs and queues](https://baselarte.com/notas/idempotency/): how to make operations safe to repeat: HTTP methods, the Idempotency-Key header, unique constraints and transactions in Postgres, queue and webhook deduplication, how to test it (including concurrency) and how to run it in production.
- [Postgres for developers](https://baselarte.com/notas/postgres-for-devs/): relational databases 80/20 focused on Postgres — schemas, connecting, roles and passwords, access security, CTEs and window functions, indexes, UUIDs, full-text search, grants, backups (3-2-1) and caching, with a Docker lab.
- [Full-stack platform case study](https://baselarte.com/notas/full-stack-engineering/): engineering notes on a real front end and back end: API-first, layered caching, session security, direct uploads, batched analytics and tests.
- [Sitemap](https://baselarte.com/sitemap.xml)
